evidence: paper: F_n = X\,\mathcal{A}_X(U_n), \qquad \mathcal{S}_n = q^{\,1-A+\lambda_n} F_n, \qquad \mathcal{A}_n = (\mathcal{S}_n/r)\,e_\theta, \qquad u_{z,n} = \partial_s \mathcal{S}_n, \qquad r\,u_{r,n} = -\partial_z \mathcal{S}_n.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same five formulas, re-encoded in two routine ways. (i) Lean's primitive object is H = S/s = q^{-A+λ_n} 𝒜_X(U_n) (prefixStream / streamFactor, exponent -CoordinateAlgebra.A h + slowOrder h n with A h = 1/2+h and slowOrder h n = 2nh = λ_n); multiplying by s and using s = qX (SimilarityProfile.X) and F_n = X 𝒜_X(U_n) (primitive_eq_mul_average) gives exactly S_n = q^{1-A+λ_n} F_n, and integratedStream is that product. (ii) The two velocity identities are stated for the finite prefix sum over n ≤ J rather than per order n: prefixStream_axial reads H + s ∂_s H = u_z, which is the product rule for ∂_s(sH) = ∂_s S, and prefixStream_flux reads -s ∂_z H = flux = r u_r, which is -∂_z(sH) = -∂_z S since s does not depend on z; slowVelocity_components identifies flux/r with u_r and slowAxial with u_z. The prefix identities are proved termwise (Finset.sum_congr), but I found no declaration stating them for a single order n.
